page: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the Epdsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 3780 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation with Clang all scoring in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching uncached large-block read speeds of 465.82 GB/sec and write speeds of 203.93 GB/sec. The server also demonstrates strong database capabilities, scoring in the top tier for PassMark database operations and achieving 117.06 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Single-core performance sits in the average tier across Geekbench and stress-ng tests.

Utilizing the ARM64 architecture, the E64pds_v6 offers high resource density and qualitative cost-efficiency for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent performance without virtualization overhead. However, the lack of AVX, AVX-512, and AMX instruction sets represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring specialized x86 vector extensions, though the platform maintains strong performance in cryptography with native AES support.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio, large local storage, and top-tier multi-threaded performance, this server is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, memory-intensive applications, multi-threaded software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
